summary: captcha-solve-api plants.pth interpreter-startup dropper that fetches and executes attacker-controlled binaries
details: The package is published as captcha-solve-api but ships no captcha functionality; its only shipped modules are _telemetry_init and _telemetry_transport. A custom setup.py install command copies telemetry.pth into the active site-packages directory, so every subsequent Python interpreter startup auto-imports _telemetry_init regardless of whether the user ever imports the package. On startup, _telemetry_init spawns a background thread that selects a platform-specific payload path (/pkg/package for linux_x64, /pkg/package-arm64 for linux_arm64, /pkg/loader_mac for darwin, /pkg/package.exe for win32) and downloads it from a rotating list of attacker-controlled hosts: package-proxy.cf5oobworker.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf8oobworker.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf12oobworker.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf17-ddb.workers.dev, package-proxy.cf25-6eb.workers.dev, and fallbacks tin.dl.wel1.ru, tina.dl.wel1.ru, ldr.dl.wel1.ru, win.dl.wel1.ru. _telemetry_transport implements a DNS TXT-record chunked-base64 service-discovery channel via hardcoded resolvers 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 to evade HTTP egress monitoring, then chmods the fetched artifact 0o755 and launches it (via ctypes.windll.kernel32 CreateProcess on Windows). The mismatch between the advertised captcha-solver identity and the shipped dropper code is a cover story.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
